ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a rectangle with $AB=3$ and $BC=4$. Point $P$ is a moving point on line segment $BC$, and point $M$ is a point on line segment $AP$ such that $\angle ADM=\angle BAP$. What is the minimum value of $BM$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, let O be the midpoint of AD and connect OB and OM.\\
$\because$ Quadrilateral ABCD is a rectangle,\\
$\therefore\angle$BAD$=90^\circ$, AD$=$BC$=4$,\\
$\therefore\angle$BAP$+\angle$DAM$=90^\circ$,\\
$\because\angle$ADM$=\angle$BAP,\\
$\therefore\angle$ADM$+\angle$DAM$=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore\angle$AMD$=90^\circ$,\\
$\because$AO$=$OD$=2$,\\
$\therefore$OM$= \frac{1}{2}$AD$=2$,\\
$\therefore$ the trajectory of point M is a circle $\odot$O with O as the center and 2 as the radius.\\
$\because$OB$= \sqrt{AB^{2}+AO^{2}} = \sqrt{3^{2}+2^{2}} = \sqrt{13}$,\\
$\therefore$BM$\geq$OB$-$OM$=\sqrt{13}-2$,\\
$\therefore$ the minimum value of BM is $\boxed{\sqrt{13}-2}$.

method.CoT_raw:
先描述图像：图中是一个长方形ABCD，A在左上、B在左下、C在右下、D在右上；P在底边BC上；从A向P画了一条线段，点M在AP上；图中还画出了与M、D相关的线段，并要求满足∠ADM=∠BAP，目标是求BM的最小值。

按指定坐标法：取B=(0,0)，A=(0,3)，C=(4,0)，D=(4,3)，令P=(p,0)，其中0≤p≤4。对p>0，直线AP的斜率为-3/p，所以AP方程为 y=3-(3/p)x。因为∠BAP是AP与竖直方向AB所成的角，所以 tan∠BAP=p/3。又∠ADM=∠BAP，且AD水平，因此过D的直线DM相对水平线的斜率为p/3，方程为 y-3=(p/3)(x-4)。

联立两条直线：3-(3/p)x=3+(p/3)(x-4)。化简得 x=4p^2/(p^2+9)，再代回AP得 y=3-12p/(p^2+9)。因此M=(4p^2/(p^2+9), 3-12p/(p^2+9))。

于是 BM^2=x^2+y^2。化简可得 BM^2=17+8(p^2-9p-9)/(p^2+9)。设 f(p)=BM^2，则 f'(p)=72(p^2+4p-9)/(p^2+9)^2。令f'(p)=0，得 p=-2±√13，其中区间[0,4]内的临界点是 p=√13-2。因为f'(p)在该点前为负、后为正，所以这里取得最小值。代入得 f_min=17-4√13=(√13-2)^2，因此 BM_min=√13-2。p=0或p=4端点对应的BM值都更大，所以最小值成立。

按指定坐标法：取B=(0,0)，A=(0,3)，C=(4,0)，D=(4,3)，令P=(p,0)，其中0≤p≤4。对p>0，直线AP的斜率为-3/p，所以AP方程为 y=3-(3/p)x。因为∠BAP是AP与竖直方向AB所成的角，所以 tan∠BAP=p/3。又∠ADM=∠BAP，且AD水平，因此过D的直线DM相对水平线的斜率为p/3，方程为 y-3=(p/3)(x-4)。

联立两条直线：3-(3/p)x=3+(p/3)(x-4)。化简得 x=4p^2/(p^2+9)，再代回AP得 y=3-12p/(p^2+9)。因此M=(4p^2/(p^2+9), 3-12p/(p^2+9))。

于是 BM^2=x^2+y^2。化简可得 BM^2=17+8(p^2-9p-9)/(p^2+9)。设 f(p)=BM^2，则 f'(p)=72(p^2+4p-9)/(p^2+9)^2。令f'(p)=0，得 p=-2±√13，其中区间[0,4]内的临界点是 p=√13-2。因为f'(p)在该点前为负、后为正，所以这里取得最小值。代入得 f_min=17-4√13=(√13-2)^2，因此 BM_min=√13-2。p=0或p=4端点对应的BM值都更大，所以最小值成立。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is an analytic-coordinate optimization route. It does not rely on recognizing the circle locus first; instead it parameterizes P, derives M explicitly from line equations, and minimizes BM algebraically.
planner_metadata.image_role: Use the image to choose a coordinate system matching the displayed rectangle, with A upper left, B lower left, C lower right, D upper right, P on BC, and M on AP connected to D.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use AB=3 and BC=4 to assign coordinates; use P moving on BC to set P=(p,0); use M on AP and ∠ADM=∠BAP to derive the two equations defining M.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Coordinate geometry; tangent/slope interpretation of an angle in a right rectangle; solving simultaneous line equations; minimizing a one-variable distance function over a closed interval.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a rectangle with $AB=3$ and $BC=4$. Point $P$ is a moving point on line segment $BC$, and point $M$ is a point on line segment $AP$ such that $\angle ADM=\angle BAP$. What is the minimum value of $BM$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, let $O$ be the midpoint of $AD$ and connect $OB$ and $OM$.\\
$\because$ quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a rectangle,\\
$\therefore \angle BAD=90^\circ$, $AD=BC=4$,\\
$\therefore \angle BAP+\angle DAM=90^\circ$,\\
$\because \angle ADM=\angle BAP$,\\
$\therefore \angle ADM+\angle DAM=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle AMD=90^\circ$,\\
$\because AO=OD=2$,\\
$\therefore OM=\frac{1}{2}AD=2$,\\
$\therefore$ the trajectory of point $M$ is a circle $\odot O$ with $O$ as the center and $2$ as the radius.\\
$\because OB=\sqrt{AB^{2}+AO^{2}}=\sqrt{3^{2}+2^{2}}=\sqrt{13}$,\\
$\therefore BM\geq OB-OM=\sqrt{13}-2$,\\
$\therefore$ the minimum value of $BM$ is $\boxed{\sqrt{13}-2}$.
raw_record.final_cot:
In the image, ABCD is a rectangle, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, D is at the upper right; P is located on the bottom side BC; a slanted line is drawn from A to P, and point M is on AP; the figure also draws the line segments from D to M and from B to M. According to the problem, AB=3, BC=4, and ∠ADM=∠BAP.

Because ABCD is a rectangle, AD⊥AB, and AD=BC=4. Also because M is on AP, AM and AP are the same straight line, therefore ∠BAP and ∠DAM are complementary, that is, ∠BAP+∠DAM=90°. It is known that ∠ADM=∠BAP, so ∠ADM+∠DAM=90°. In triangle ADM, the third angle ∠AMD=90°.

Therefore M lies on the circle with AD as diameter. Let O be the midpoint of AD, then AO=OD=2, so the center of this circle is O, and the radius OM=2. Now we need to minimize BM, that is, find the minimum distance from the fixed point B to point M on this circle. The nearest distance equals BO minus the radius 2.

In right triangle BAO, BA=3, AO=2, so BO=√(3²+2²)=√13. Therefore the minimum value of BM is BO−OM=√13−2.
